title: What are confidence intervals and why do we need them?

cues.en: Instructor: I'm going to begin this section on confidence intervals by going on vacation, but don't worry, you're gonna come with me.
cues.zh: 講師：信賴區間這一章，要先去度假開場，但別擔心，你也一起來。

cues.en: Remember a while back in the course, I claimed that the true population height of Montenegrins is 182 centimeters, or maybe I said 183, I don't remember,
cues.zh: 記得之前聲稱蒙特內哥羅人的真正母體身高是 182 公分，或也許說 183，不記得了，

cues.en: but it's somewhere around here.
cues.zh: 反正大約在這附近。

cues.en: Now, you and I are going to confirm this.
cues.zh: 現在你我一起確認。

cues.en: We're gonna go to Montenegro, and before we do our really important scientific research, we're gonna take a couple weeks and try out the local cuisine, check out the bars,
cues.zh: 去蒙特內哥羅，在重要科學研究前，先花幾週嘗當地美食、逛酒吧，

cues.en: and do some hiking, hang out at the beach.
cues.zh: 健行、到海邊放鬆。

cues.en: And then after a few weeks of that, we're gonna get down to real serious science.
cues.zh: 幾週後，再開始認真做科學。

cues.en: And to save time, we're going to split up.
cues.zh: 為省時間，分頭進行。

cues.en: So I'm going to do study one, and you are going to do study two.
cues.zh: 我做研究一，你做研究二。

cues.en: So I'm going to go around Montenegro and just find 10 random adults and measure their height.
cues.zh: 我到處隨機找 10 位成年人，量身高。

cues.en: And then I'm gonna find 10 other randomly selected adults and measure their height and repeat that 500 times.
cues.zh: 再找另外 10 位，重複 500 次。

cues.en: So I'm going to get 500 repetitions of 10 randomly selected people.
cues.zh: 得到 500 次，每次 10 位隨機選取的人。

cues.en: Now you think that you're better than me and maybe you are in this doing research like this.
cues.zh: 你認為比我厲害，做這種研究也許確實如此。

cues.en: So you actually go out and you do the same experiment, but you get 80 randomly selected people instead of 10.
cues.zh: 做相同實驗，但每次隨機找 80 位，不是 10 位。

cues.en: So you measure the heights of 80, randomly selected Montenegrins, and then you find 80 more randomly selected Montenegrins, and you keep repeating that 500 times, okay?
cues.zh: 量 80 位隨機選的蒙特內哥羅人，再找 80 位，重複 500 次。

cues.en: And then it takes quite a while, it takes us a couple weeks to gather all this data and then we come back and we compare notes, we compare our data sets.
cues.zh: 收資料花了幾週，再回來比對筆記和資料集。

cues.en: So then what we can look at is the distributions of our sample heights.
cues.zh: 可以看樣本身高分布。

cues.en: Now, we already know from the central limit theorem that our distributions are going to be roughly Gaussian.
cues.zh: 根據中央極限定理，知道分布會大致高斯。

cues.en: And we know that because we're not comparing the actual numbers.
cues.zh: 因為比較的不是實際數字，

cues.en: Each individual person that we measured.
cues.zh: 不是每個量測的個人。

cues.en: Instead, you and I are going to compare the distribution of 500 average heights that we got from my samples of 10
cues.zh: 而是比較我的 10 人樣本，

cues.en: and your samples of 80.
cues.zh: 和你的 80 人樣本，各自取得的 500 個平均身高分布。

cues.en: So let's imagine they look something like this.
cues.zh: 假設像這樣。

cues.en: Now notice that the peaks of both of these distributions are more or less at the same value, and that we expect from the law of large numbers.
cues.zh: 兩分布峰大致位於相同值，這是根據大數法則預期的。

cues.en: The question is who is more confident about their results?
cues.zh: 誰對結果更有信心？

cues.en: You or me?
cues.zh: 你還是我？

cues.en: Well, it's pretty obvious that you can be more confident about your results because you measured more people here.
cues.zh: 顯然你更有信心，因為測更多人。

cues.en: So your distribution is actually going to be narrower.
cues.zh: 所以分布會更窄。

cues.en: You see yours as a narrower peak here.
cues.zh: 你的峰比較窄。

cues.en: I get the same average of averages, but you can see my distributions, the distribution of my data is quite a bit wider.
cues.zh: 我的平均值之平均相同，但資料分布寬很多。

cues.en: So there were times where I sampled 10 people and those 10 people happened to be pretty short, and I got an average height of like 158 centimeters
cues.zh: 有時抽 10 人，剛好都矮，得到像 158 公分的平均身高，

cues.en: and you didn't really get that at all.
cues.zh: 你卻幾乎沒遇到。

cues.en: So this is qualitative.
cues.zh: 這是定性觀察。

cues.en: Here we see my distribution, your distribution, and qualitatively we can say that you should be more confident about your results compared to me
cues.zh: 我的分布和你的分布，定性而言，你應該比我更有信心，

cues.en: because your distribution is narrower and that's because you measured more people, okay?
cues.zh: 因為分布窄，而那是因為測更多人。

cues.en: So this is like kind of the idea of confidence intervals.
cues.zh: 有點像信賴區間的概念。

cues.en: It's not exactly the correct interpretation.
cues.zh: 不是完全正確的解讀。

cues.en: I'm gonna give you the formal definition in a little bit, but this is the idea.
cues.zh: 稍後給正式定義，但概念如此。

cues.en: You measured more data, you have a narrower distribution, and so you can be more confident than I can be because I measured overall less data.
cues.zh: 測更多資料、分布更窄，所以比測量資料較少的我更有信心。

cues.en: I had smaller sample sizes, okay?
cues.zh: 我的樣本數較小。

cues.en: So the way that confidence intervals are typically quantified is by estimating this distribution or computing it empirically
cues.zh: 通常量化信賴區間，是估計或實際計算這個分布，

cues.en: and then taking 95% of this distribution.
cues.zh: 再取其中 95%。

cues.en: Oh yeah.
cues.zh: 喔，對。

cues.en: So this, I already said many samples gave the wrong answer.
cues.zh: 這個，已經說過，很多樣本給出錯誤答案。

cues.en: Okay, so here we have the 95% confidence interval.
cues.zh: 這裡是 95% 信賴區間。

cues.en: So based on the distribution of all of these different experiments, we can say that this is the 95% confidence interval for my study.
cues.zh: 根據不同實驗的分布，這是我的研究的 95% 信賴區間。

cues.en: This is the 95% confidence interval for your study.
cues.zh: 這是你的研究的 95% 信賴區間。

cues.en: Now you have a much smaller confidence interval for the same level of confidence compared to me.
cues.zh: 相同信心水準下，你的區間比我小很多。

cues.en: So we can be a little bit more confident in your estimate of the average height and a little bit less confident about my estimate of the average Montenegro height.
cues.zh: 所以對你的平均身高估計更有信心，對我的稍微沒那麼有信心。

cues.en: Okay, so I hope that builds up some intuition and I hope you are inspired to go on holiday in Montenegro or at least look up pictures.
cues.zh: 希望建立了一些直覺，也希望讓你想去蒙特內哥羅度假，至少查查照片。

cues.en: I'd never been there, but it looks like a really beautiful country.
cues.zh: 我沒去過，但看起來很美。

cues.en: Anyway, here is a definition of the confidence interval.
cues.zh: 這裡是信賴區間定義。

cues.en: So the confidence interval is the probability that an unknown population parameter falls within a range of values in repeated samples of that same experiment.
cues.zh: 信賴區間是，在重複相同實驗的樣本中，未知母體參數落在某範圍內的機率。

cues.en: It's a little bit of a tricky interpretation because the way that you want to interpret it is that confidence intervals tell you how confident you can be
cues.zh: 解讀有點棘手，因為你想把它解讀為，對真正母體參數

cues.en: that the true population parameter lies within your confidence interval.
cues.zh: 位於你的區間內，有多少信心。

cues.en: That's kind of the the naive initial intuition, but unfortunately it's a little bit more complicated than that.
cues.zh: 這是最初直覺，但可惜稍微更複雜。

cues.en: So what the confidence interval really represents is your confidence in future experiments that repeat your experiments, so independent replications of your experiment,
cues.zh: 真正表示的是，對未來重複實驗、獨立重複驗證的信心，

cues.en: and how likely it is that the population parameter will fall within the confidence interval in those future experiments.
cues.zh: 以及在那些未來實驗中，母體參數落在信賴區間內的可能性。

cues.en: I know it sounds a little weird, the video at the end of this section.
cues.zh: 知道聽起來奇怪，本章最後的影片，

cues.en: So the last video in this section is gonna be all about misconceptions of confidence intervals and I hope that as you go throughout this section,
cues.zh: 會專談信賴區間的誤解，希望隨著本章進行，

cues.en: it will become a little bit more fine-grained and intuitive, what the confidence interval actually does and does not reflect.
cues.zh: 你能更細緻、直觀地理解它反映什麼、不反映什麼。

cues.en: Okay, so this is a statement here is a little bit of math.
cues.zh: 這裡用一點數學表達。

cues.en: So L is the lower boundary from the confidence interval.
cues.zh: L 是信賴區間下界。

cues.en: U is the upper boundary of the confidence interval, and C is our proportion, our confidence interval, which in the previous slide I said was 95%.
cues.zh: U 是上界，C 是比例、信賴水準，上一張說 95%。

cues.en: So you can call that 0.95 mu of course is the population mean or whatever is the population parameter and P is the probability.
cues.zh: 可稱為 0.95；μ 當然是母體平均，或其他母體參數，P 是機率。

cues.en: So we say that the probability that the population parameter is between the lower bound and the upper bound of the confidence interval is 0.95 or 95%
cues.zh: 在大量未來重複當前實驗的研究中，母體參數位於下界與上界之間的機率，為 0.95、95%，

cues.en: in a large number of future experiments that replicate the current experiment.
cues.zh: 也就是許多未來重複實驗中的機率。

cues.en: So I picked 95% in the previous slide.
cues.zh: 上一張選 95%。

cues.en: It's a little bit arbitrary of course, I've mentioned before these thresholds are always a little bit arbitrary in statistics,
cues.zh: 有點任意，之前提過，統計中的門檻總有一點任意，

cues.en: but typical confidence intervals are 95% or 99%.
cues.zh: 但常見信賴區間為 95% 或 99%。

cues.en: 90% I think is a little bit less common, but I suppose you do see it sometimes.
cues.zh: 90% 比較少見，但偶爾也有。

cues.en: Mostly people report 95% confidence intervals.
cues.zh: 大部分報告 95%。

cues.en: Okay, this is just an expansion on this definition here.
cues.zh: 這只是擴充這裡的定義。

cues.en: So the proportion of a large number of samples that will include the population parameter within its confidence interval.
cues.zh: 大量樣本中，信賴區間包含母體參數的比例。

cues.en: Again, the confidence interval is telling us about our confidence that future experiments will contain the same confidence intervals and that the population parameter
cues.zh: 再次提醒，它告訴我們，對未來實驗會有相同信賴區間，以及母體參數

cues.en: will be within those intervals.
cues.zh: 位於那些區間內的信心。

cues.en: So what I'd like to do now is list some of the factors that influence the size of the confidence intervals.
cues.zh: 接著列出影響區間大小的因素。

cues.en: So some of the factors that change whether the confidence intervals are relatively narrow or relatively wide.
cues.zh: 讓區間較窄或較寬的因素。

cues.en: Now, one of these factors I've already mentioned in our thought experiment where we go on holiday to Montenegro and that is the sample size
cues.zh: 其中一個，在蒙特內哥羅度假思想實驗中已提過，就是樣本數，

cues.en: and basically confidence intervals are influenced by the sample size and by the variance of the data.
cues.zh: 基本上，信賴區間受樣本數與資料變異數影響。

cues.en: And I think both of these are pretty intuitive as the sample size increases, the confidence intervals decrease.
cues.zh: 兩者很直觀，樣本數增加，信賴區間縮小。

cues.en: So the boundaries, the confidence intervals get closer to each other.
cues.zh: 邊界彼此更靠近。

cues.en: And you can probably also guess what the story is for variance, as the variance gets smaller, so the variability in the data gets smaller, the confidence intervals also get closer to each other.
cues.zh: 變異數的情況也猜得到，資料變異越小，區間同樣越靠近。

cues.en: There are two methods for computing confidence intervals, one based on applying formulas and one based on empirical bootstrapping or resampling
cues.zh: 計算有兩種方法，一種套公式，一種透過經驗拔靴、重新抽樣，

cues.en: and you'll learn both of these methods over the next few videos.
cues.zh: 接下來幾部會學到兩種。
